notes: Blaenau Gwent has no selective or additional licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies, for properties of three or more storeys with five or more occupants in more than one household. All landlords in Wales must also register with Rent Smart Wales.
research: NEGATIVE, sourced. The council's HMO page recites all three Housing Act 2004 regimes generically and never claims to have exercised any: additional licensing is described only as 'A discretionary power that councils may decide to apply to a particular type of HMO', and selective as 'This is where the council MAY declare that certain areas, for example, where there is low demand for housing and/or antisocial behaviour, are appropriate for selective licensing.' A textbook statutory-powers recital, and the single reason a keyword scan flags this council. The only licensable category actually stated is the Welsh mandatory test: 'Three or more storeys high / Have five or more people in more than one household, and / Share amenities such as bathrooms, toilets and cooking facilities.' Applications are handed off to GOV.UK; there is no local scheme application route. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the approved 'Council Wide Fees and Charges 2026/2027' register contains exactly one HMO row, 'Public Protection - Housing | HMO License | 5 Yearly License Fee | £329.90 (2025/2026) | £339.80 (2026/2027)', with zero occurrences of 'selective', 'additional licen' or 'multiple occup' elsewhere in it. Corroborated by two current strategy documents: the Private Sector Housing Renewal Policy 2025-2030 mentions licensing exactly once and only as Rent Smart Wales; the Housing Strategy and Action Plan 2025-2030 (adopted Dec 2025) mentions HMOs once with no designation or proposal. ModernGov was CONTROL-VALIDATED ('zzqqxx' = 0 document hits, 'housing' = 20); 'selective licensing' and 'additional licensing' returned only committee-name matches, Licensing Act 2003 and animal-licensing items. Sitemap sweep covered 987 URLs across /en/ and /cy/ with no licensing-scheme page. TRAPS EXCLUDED: the statutory-powers recital above; the s.254 HMO definition; Rent Smart Wales; the Welsh mandatory three-storey test (WSI 2006/1712 (W.174)); the fee row 'Notices under s49 Housing Act 2004' (£277.30 per notice, enforcement cost recovery not licensing); and the Welsh homonyms, where all 13 'ychwanegol' hits are 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' (Additional Learning Needs) and the single 'dewisol' hit is 'addysg ddewisol yn y cartref' (elective home education). LIMITATION: the council's own site search is unusable server-side ('council tax', 'zzqqxx', 'selective licensing' and 'HMO' all returned byte-identical 158,661-byte responses), so it is client-side rendered and a nil result there proves nothing. The conclusion rests on the sitemap sweep, the fee register, the two policy PDFs and the control-validated committee search.

notes: Bridgend has no selective or additional licensing scheme and says so in its own guidance. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys, five or more occupants, more than one household. Fee £792, or £657 to renew. Rent Smart Wales is separate.
research: NEGATIVE, and the council states it explicitly. Appendix 3 to Bridgend's Houses in Multiple Occupation Supplementary Planning Guidance, before Cabinet 03/02/2026, Council 04/02/2026 and Development Control Committee 05/02/2026, says under its Licensing heading: 'Mandatory HMO licensing: properties with 5 or more residents forming more than one household; comprising three or more storeys; and sharing basic amenities. / Additional or selective licensing schemes for smaller HMOs (not applied by Bridgend County Borough Council).' Licensing is delivered by Shared Regulatory Services, the joint statutory service of Bridgend, Cardiff and the Vale of Glamorgan, linked directly from bridgend.gov.uk. The SRS HMO hub states: 'If your HMO has 3 or more storeys with five or more occupants made up of at least two households and is located anywhere in Cardiff, Vale of Glamorgan or Bridgend area you will need a Mandatory HMO Licence. If you own or manage a HMO of any type or size in the Cathays or Plasnewydd area of Cardiff which is not subject to mandatory licensing, you will need to apply for an Additional HMO Licence. Similarly, if you own or manage a HMO which isn't subject to mandatory licensing in the Castleland Renewal Area in Vale of Glamorgan, you will need to apply for an Additional Licence. There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' Bridgend is named for mandatory only. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the SRS 'HMO Licensing in Bridgend' page gives the full ladder effective 1 April 2026 as 'Mandatory HMO Licence Fee: £792 / Mandatory HMO Licence Fee (Renewal): £657' with no small-HMO or per-property tier, and only two forms. Bridgend's corporate Licensing Fees 2026-27 spreadsheet has 12 sheets and zero HMO or housing rows. The Cardiff page on the same SRS site is a useful contrast control: where additional licensing exists, SRS names it and gives it its own fee ladder, so Bridgend's silence is meaningful rather than an omission. Independently verified: Bridgend's own 129KB HTML sitemap contains zero occurrences of 'selective licen' or 'additional licen', and its only 'Multiple Occupation' entry is a planning item. The A-to-Z passed a control and letter S contained no 'Selective' entry. ModernGov was CONTROL-VALIDATED ('zzqqxx' = 0, 'housing' = 29); 'selective licensing' returned only the HMO Supplementary Planning Guidance items. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Cardiff's Cathays and Plasnewydd additional licensing and the Vale's Castleland Renewal Area additional licensing, all published on the SAME SRS website and by far the biggest misattribution risk here; the HMO Supplementary Planning Guidance itself; the s.254 definition; Rent Smart Wales; the Welsh mandatory three-storey test. The Welsh site licensing index returned 47 'trwydd' hits but zero for 'dewisol', 'dethol', 'ychwanegol' or 'amlfedd'. LIMITATION: bridgend.moderngov.co.uk returned HTTP 522 on three attempts with browser headers, a genuine outage not a bot block; it is a stale host and the live system was searched successfully with validated controls.

notes: Caerphilly has no selective or additional licensing scheme. The council states licensing is restricted to HMOs of three or more storeys housing five or more tenants from two or more families. Fee £250 for five years. Rent Smart Wales registration is separate.
research: NEGATIVE, sourced twice over. The council's HMO page states, in its own words: 'Certain HMOs are required to be licensed by the council, however very few actually exist within the county borough. Licensing is restricted to HMOs that are 3 or more storeys in height and house 5 or more tenants, made up from 2 or more families.' The phrase 'Licensing is restricted to', followed by the Welsh mandatory threshold, affirmatively excludes any wider designation. This page was read in a rendered browser session, reached through the real link graph (Housing > Private housing > Houses in multiple occupation); the raw page contains zero occurrences of 'additional licen' or 'selective licen'. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: 'We currently operate a mandatory licensing scheme and the fee is £250 for 5 years.' A single flat mandatory fee with no per-property or small-HMO tier and no separate application route; a self-financing s.56 or Part 3 designation could not exist without its own cost-recovery fee. Wayback shows stability rather than recent change: the fee sentence is byte-stable across snapshots of 23 Jul 2019, 25 Mar 2023 and 20 May 2024, and the HMO page has zero instances of 'selective' or 'additional licensing' in snapshots of 17 Jul 2016, 21 Aug 2019, 30 Mar 2023 and 26 Jan 2026. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2007' cited on the HMO page, which is the s.257 management instrument, the Welsh twin of the England 2007 regulations, not s.56; (2) 'certain additional requirements are necessary for these properties', management-standards wording; (3) on the Welsh site, 'gofynion ychwanegol' and '(Darpariaethau Ychwanegol) (Cymru) 2007', the same two traps in Welsh, with no instance of 'trwyddedu ychwanegol', 'trwyddedu dethol' or 'trwyddedu dewisol'; (4) the voluntary landlord accreditation page; (5) Housing renewal and Private Sector Renewal Strategy pages, which are grants and regeneration; (6) Rent Smart Wales. LIMITATIONS, stated plainly: caerphilly.gov.uk serves SOFT 404s (Kentico returns HTTP 200 with homepage content for unknown paths, confirmed by fetching /robots.txt and receiving the homepage), so URL guessing is actively misleading and the real link graph was navigated instead. Its site search is broken and this was proved with controls: 'council tax', 'multiple occupation', 'selective licensing' and 'zzqqxxvv' all returned exactly 47,559 bytes, so a nil result there proves nothing. caerphilly.moderngov.co.uk returns 522; democracy.caerphilly.gov.uk is up but shares the broken search behaviour, so committee papers were not full-text searchable.

schemes.areaDescription: The Cathays ward, covering every HMO of any size or type that is not already covered by mandatory licensing
The Plasnewydd ward, covering every HMO of any size not already covered by mandatory licensing

notes: In Cathays, any size of HMO needs an additional licence until 1 February 2028. The separate Plasnewydd scheme's five year term ended on 1 January 2026, but the council still lists it as running, so check with Cardiff before letting there. No selective licensing.
research: CATHAYS: primary designation instrument obtained. Cardiff's own public notice reads: 'Notice is hereby given that the City of Cardiff Council has confirmed the designation of an additional licensing scheme in respect of houses in multiple occupation covering the Cathays Community Ward. This scheme will be known as (The City of Cardiff Council's Houses in Multiple Occupation Additional Licensing Scheme 2023). The confirmation of the designation is in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. The designation was made at the Council's Cabinet Meeting on 20th October 2022... The Scheme will be effective from 1st February 2023 and unless revoked beforehand will cease to have effect on 1st February 2028.' Unambiguous s.56, live today. PLASNEWYDD, THE JUDGEMENT CALL: SRS states 'The Plasnewydd Scheme first came into effect on 3 November 2014 and again went live on 1 January 2021 for a period of 5 years.' By the council's own arithmetic, and by the exact pattern the Cathays notice uses, that term ended on 1 January 2026, seven months ago. No re-designation could be found. Every Cardiff Cabinet agenda for 2024, 2025 and 2026 was scanned (33 meetings) for 'plasnewydd', 'additional licens', 'selective licens', 'multiple occupation' and 'HMO'; the only hit was a School Organisation Planning item. That scan is CONTROL-VALIDATED, since the same parser extracts real agenda item titles from those pages, and the Cathays precedent shows Cardiff makes these designations at Cabinet. RECORDED AS EXPIRED BUT FLAGGED LOUDLY, because the council still presents it in the present tense ('Cardiff Council has declared two areas within Cardiff as Additional Licensing Schemes, namely Cathays and Plasnewydd') and the SRS hub still tells landlords in 'the Cathays or Plasnewydd area' they need an Additional HMO Licence. The linked 'Public Notice Plasnewydd HMO Licensing Scheme' is a BROKEN LINK on the council's own site, pointing at an unrelated 2020 standards document, so no Plasnewydd instrument is publicly available. The public note therefore tells a Plasnewydd landlord to check with Cardiff rather than assume they are clear. SELECTIVE LICENSING: expressly ruled out. SRS states 'There are currently no areas of selective licensing.' Cardiff's own sitemap (1,151 URLs) contains no selective or additional licensing page at all. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, strongly positive: Cardiff's ladder includes 'HMO Shared House or single flat up to 4 bedrooms: Initial Application fee £160, 2nd payment if compliant £230, Total fee compliant £390' rising to £460 at 15+ bedrooms, or £810 to £960 if non-compliant, plus per-flat surcharges. A four-bedroom tier sits BELOW the mandatory five-occupant threshold, which is exactly the small-HMO tell of a genuine s.56 scheme, and the application form is captioned 'both mandatory and additional applications can be completed on the same form'. WARDS: 'Cathays' and 'Plasnewydd' were both checked against the current ONS register via the repo's bundled wards.json and BOTH ARE CURRENT Cardiff wards, so matching is safe in both directions. TRAPS EXCLUDED: cardiff.gov.uk/HMOlicence is a PLANNING page, not licensing, opening 'This information refers to HMOs within the Planning system' before discussing use classes C4 and Sui Generis, LDP policy H5 and the 20 per cent / 10 per cent concentration thresholds for Cathays and Plasnewydd; that concentration policy is planning control and is a strong lookalike for a licensing boundary. Also excluded: the s.254 definition; Rent Smart Wales; and the Vale of Glamorgan's Castleland Renewal Area additional licensing, which appears on the same SRS site and belongs to a different council. LIMITATION: Cardiff's ModernGov document search is unusable via GET (identical empty responses for 'council tax', 'Plasnewydd', 'additional licensing' and a nonsense control), so meeting lists were browsed directly. Note also that srs.wales is not itself a .gov.uk domain; it is the statutory joint regulatory service of Cardiff, Bridgend and the Vale, and cardiff.gov.uk links to it as the authoritative HMO licensing destination.

schemes.areaDescription: The Tyisha ward of Llanelli; all privately rented properties in the area needed a licence, whether or not they were HMOs

notes: Carmarthenshire has no active selective or additional licensing. A selective scheme covered the Tyisha ward of Llanelli but ended on 2 July 2019. Only mandatory HMO licensing now applies, county-wide. One council page still wrongly describes the Tyisha scheme as live.
research: CURRENT POSITION, from the council directly: the live Licensing page (updated 04/02/2026) states 'We currently operate one licensing schemes for privately rented properties in Carmarthenshire - a mandatory licensing scheme for houses in multiple occupation (HMO)... Mandatory licensing applies across the whole of Carmarthenshire.' THE EXPIRED SELECTIVE SCHEME was found ONLY by grepping the WELSH-language page, which names the statutory type the English page conceals: 'Ar hyn o bryd rydym yn gweithredu dau gynllun trwyddedu - trwyddedu gorfodol ar gyfer tai amlfeddiannaeth a TRWYDDEDU DETHOL sy'n benodol ar gyfer Ward Ty-isa yn Llanelli.' LEXICAL POINT FOR ALL FUTURE WELSH WORK: the statutory Welsh term in use is 'trwyddedu DETHOL', not the 'trwyddedu dewisol' commonly assumed; searching only for 'dewisol' would have missed this entirely. The English twin page says only the uninformative 'licensing specific to the Tyisha Ward in Llanelli'. Archived copies of the council's own licensing page confirm type and end date verbatim and unchanged across snapshots of 1 Dec 2020, 26 Feb 2021, 18 May 2022 and 29 Mar 2023: 'We currently have one Selective Licensing Scheme in operation, in the Tyisha ward of Llanelli. It will last until July 2, 2019, and complements a Local Lettings Policy which is also in place for council housing in Tyisha.' The council left that paragraph up for roughly five years after its own stated expiry. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, which is what distinguishes a genuine Part 3 designation from boilerplate: those archived pages carry a separate cost-recovery table headed 'Licence fees within a Selective Licensing Scheme area' (Single Household Occupation £240, 2 Flats £360, 3 Flats £480, 4 Flats £600, 5 Flats £720, with LAW-affiliated discounts), together with the correct statutory description 'All privately rented properties within a selective licensing area have to be licensed, regardless of whether the property is an HMO.' Snapshot diffing dates the removal: the wording is present on 21 Apr 2024 and gone by 19 Apr 2025. START DATE NOT VERIFIED: the earliest capture of any Carmarthenshire licensing page is 1 Dec 2020. A Part 3 designation runs a statutory maximum of five years, which would imply commencement on or about 3 July 2014, but no council document states it, so it is recorded as null rather than asserted. LIVE CORROBORATION that nothing is active: the HMO public register lists only three licensed properties and every row's licence-type column reads 'Mandatory'. WARD: 'Tyisha' was checked against the current ONS register and IS a current Carmarthenshire ward, so matching is safe; the Welsh form 'Ty-isa' is not and must not be used as a key. STALE COUNCIL PAGE, FLAG THIS: the letting-your-property page (updated 21/04/2026, NEWER than the authoritative licensing page) still reads 'We currently operate two licensing schemes - mandatory licensing for houses in multiple occupation, and licensing specific to the Tyisha Ward in Llanelli.' A landlord reading only that page would wrongly conclude a selective scheme is live. The licensing page, the fee schedule and the public register all agree it is gone. TRAPS EXCLUDED: (1) 'Ward_Profile_Tyisha_polygon', which looks like a mapped designation boundary but is one entry in a generic alphabetical GIS ward-boundary layer injected into every page; (2) 'dewisol' on the Welsh housing page, which is cookie-consent boilerplate, 'Rwy'n derbyn cwcis dewisol' meaning 'I accept optional cookies'; (3) Rent Smart Wales; (4) the s.254 definition; (5) THE CURRENT MANDATORY FEE TABLE'S THREE-PERSON BAND. The live ladder runs '3: £457.70 / 4-6: £624.90 / 7-10: £793.10 / 11+: £962.50', and a three-person band looks exactly like the small-HMO tell of an additional scheme, since Welsh mandatory licensing needs five or more occupiers. It is a legacy band carried over from the Tyisha era (the identical band, then £380, appears in the 2024 snapshot alongside the selective table). Given the council's explicit 'one licensing scheme... applies across the whole of Carmarthenshire' and a register showing only Mandatory licences, it must NOT be recorded as additional licensing. LIMITATIONS: two search engines are broken and this was proved with controls rather than trusting a nil return. The council's search renders in JavaScript, returning near-identical ~181KB pages with no result links for 'council tax', 'zzqqxx', 'selective licensing' and 'HMO'. The committee search returns 'No results' even for the control query across POST and GET and all four SearchType values, so committee papers could not be full-text searched, which is precisely why the designation's start date remains unverified. carmarthenshire.gov.uk no longer resolves and /sitemap.xml 404s; the site tree was enumerated through the Umbraco nav API, which exposed the otherwise unlinked /business/landlords/ branch where the answer lives.

schemes.areaDescription: The whole county for HMOs with five or more people in two or more households (any number of storeys) and for converted flats; in the Aberystwyth and Llanbadarn Fawr area it also catches HMOs with three or more people in three or more households

notes: Ceredigion runs additional HMO licensing from 10 July 2024 to 9 July 2029. County-wide it covers HMOs with five or more people in two or more households, whatever the number of storeys, plus converted flats. Around Aberystwyth it also covers three or more people.
research: ACTIVE s.56 scheme, designation instrument obtained. CRITICAL SCOPING POINT: the common assumption that this is an 'Aberystwyth-only' student scheme is WRONG and dangerously so. The designation has two limbs. Paragraph 4(a) applies a three-or-more-persons / three-or-more-households test in eight Aberystwyth-area wards. Paragraph 4(b) applies to 'The whole of the County of Ceredigion' for HMOs with five or more persons in two or more households (ANY number of storeys, so it bites below the Welsh mandatory three-storey test) and for s.257 converted flats. Recording this with coverage 'wards' would falsely clear every landlord in Cardigan, Lampeter, Aberaeron and New Quay, so it is recorded as borough-wide with wards null, and the stricter Aberystwyth tier is described in areaDescription instead. WARD STALENESS, THE REASON WARDS ARE NULL: although made on 19 March 2024, the designation reuses PRE-2022 ward names and its Annex A map is stamped 'Printed on: 2018-11-28'. The eight named are Aberystwyth Bronglais, Aberystwyth Central, Aberystwyth North, Aberystwyth Penparcau, Aberystwyth Rheidol, Faenor, Llanbadarn Fawr Padarn and Llanbadarn Fawr Sulien. All eight were checked against the current ONS register via the repo's bundled wards.json: FIVE NO LONGER EXIST (Aberystwyth Bronglais, Aberystwyth Central, Aberystwyth North, Llanbadarn Fawr Padarn, Llanbadarn Fawr Sulien); only Aberystwyth Penparcau, Aberystwyth Rheidol and Faenor survive. The current register instead carries 'Aberystwyth Morfa a Glais' and a single 'Llanbadarn Fawr'. Putting that list in the wards field would have produced silent mismatches in both directions. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the 1 April 2026 schedule carries a SEPARATE line, 'Additional HMO licensing fee per habitable room (for those not subject to mandatory fee) - New Licence £334.00 / Renewal £281.00', alongside the distinct mandatory line, with a 50 per cent discount for ANUK-compliant university HMOs; the application form is titled 'Mandatory and Additional Licensing Application Form'. THREE EXPIRED PREDECESSORS establish a long-running rolling regime: 2009-04-01 to 2014-03-31 (county-wide); 2014-04-14 to 2019-04-13 (Aberystwyth, Llanbadarn Fawr, Borth, Llanfarian and LAMPETER, which was covered then and is not in the three-person tier now); and 2019-04-14 to 2024-04-14. There is a genuine gap of about three months between the third and fourth designations caused by the three-month notice requirement, which is why the current start is 10 July 2024 rather than mid-April. MOST DANGEROUS TRAP FOUND: Ceredigion's own Additional Licensing Review 2023, page 11, contains the phrase 'The Housing Act 2004 (SELECTIVE Licensing) (Wales) General Approval 2007'. This is a COUNCIL TYPO. The same sentence continues '...may introduce an ADDITIONAL Licensing Scheme without obtaining Assembly approval', and the designation instrument itself cites the correct '(Additional HMO Licensing) (Wales) General Approval 2007'. A keyword search would misread this as a live Part 3 scheme; Ceredigion has never operated selective licensing. OTHER TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales; Welsh mandatory HMO licensing under WSI 2006/1712 (W.174), which because of the retained three-storey element already catches many Aberystwyth student houses independently; the s.254 definitional recitals; statutory-power recitals; per-room surcharges; and Article 4 and planning permission requirements discussed for Aberystwyth. The s.257 coverage is NOT the England '(Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' trap: the instrument cites the Wales 2006 Regulations and s.56 directly. LIMITATIONS: Ceredigion's ModernGov search returns blank forms, worked around via cabinet papers on the corporate site; the 2019 designation PDF is gone from both the live site and Wayback, so the third scheme's dates rest on the cabinet report, and the council's own documents are internally inconsistent about it. The council's site search itself passed its control tests, and sitemap raw-HTML greps for 'selectiv' and 'dewisol' returned zero, backed by a Wayback CDX sweep showing no selective-licensing URL ever existed on the domain.

schemes.areaDescription: Pensarn (Marine Road and South Parade only), Colwyn Bay (Glyn and Rhiw areas only) and Llandudno and Craig y Don (Gogarth Mostyn, Tudno and Craig-y-don areas only)

notes: Conwy runs additional HMO licensing in parts of Pensarn, Colwyn Bay and Llandudno and Craig y Don, where an HMO of any size needs a licence. The 2026-27 fee is £1,398 for up to four lets. Conwy does not publish the scheme dates, so confirm the boundary with the council.
research: ACTIVE, established from Conwy's own live licensing page: 'Under our Additional Licensing Scheme there is a different criteria. Additional Licensing only applies to buildings within certain areas of Conwy County. These areas are: Pensarn (Marine Road and South Parade only); Colwyn Bay (within the electoral divisions of Glyn and Rhiw wards only); Llandudno and Craig y Don (within the electoral divisions of Gogarth Mostyn, Tudno and Craig y Don wards only). An HMO in the areas named above must have a licence if: there are three or more tenants living in the building OR they form more than one household, with shared facilities or without shared facilities (typically self-contained flats); the building does not meet the 1991 Building Regulations; Less than two thirds of the self-contained flats are owner occupied.' It separately states the mandatory test, so the two regimes are clearly distinguished. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive and the reason this is recorded active rather than expired: the page carries a live schedule headed 'Fees are valid from 1 April 2026' with a SEPARATE additional-licensing tier: 'Mandatory licensing: up to 4 lets £819, additional lets over 4 (per let) £145. Additional licensing: up to 4 lets £1,398, additional lets over 4 (per let) £286', with instalment options and worked examples to seven lets (£2,256). A council does not publish a distinct, higher, current-financial-year cost-recovery fee for a designation that has lapsed. DATES NOT PUBLISHED: Conwy publishes no designation notice for the current areas, so start and end are null rather than guessed. The live site was searched for 'designation', 'public notice', 'Pensarn' and 'Craig y Don licensing' and no instrument was found. This is an honest gap and the public note tells landlords to confirm the boundary with the council. SELECTIVE LICENSING: ruled out on a CONTROL-VALIDATED search, which matters because most Conwy tooling is broken. Conwy's site search passes BOTH controls: the positive control 'council tax' returns real relevant results, and the negative control 'zzqqxxvv' returns 'Your search did not match any content.' Against that validated engine, 'selective licensing' ALSO returns 'Your search did not match any content', so that nil result is meaningful. 'multiple occupation', 'HMO' and 'additional licensing' all correctly surface the HMO licensing page, confirming the index covers it. THE EXPIRED PREDECESSOR: Conwy's archived public notice reads 'Notice is hereby given that Conwy County Borough Council has on the 29th day of October 2019 designated an additional licensing scheme in respect of Houses in Multiple Occupation for the electoral ward of Abergele Pensarn... The Scheme will be effective from 1st January 2020 and unless revoked beforehand or extended will cease to have effect on 31st December 2024', citing the Wales 2006 Regulations and s.58(1)(b) and (7). That page now returns 'This page is no longer available'. It is not recorded as a separate scheme object because it is superseded by the current street-based designation covering the same locality. WARDS DELIBERATELY NULL. Checked against the current ONS register: 'Abergele Pensarn' NO LONGER EXISTS (now 'Pen-sarn Pentre Mawr' and 'Gele and Llanddulas'). For the live scheme, Glyn, Rhiw, Gogarth Mostyn and Tudno ARE current Conwy wards, but 'Craig y Don' as the council spells it is not: ONS carries 'Craig-y-don', hyphenated, so an exact-match lookup fails on punctuation alone. More importantly the Pensarn limb is defined by STREETS and the Colwyn Bay and Llandudno limbs are expressly sub-ward ('only'), so a ward list must not be synthesised. Coverage 'areas' with wards null routes these to a boundary check rather than a confident wrong answer in either direction. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales, the ONLY licensing regime Conwy's landlord pages mention; 'Additional grant funding of up to £25,000' under Leasing Scheme Wales, a grant not a licence; 'an additional charge of £50' for late applications; 'The Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation (Additional Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2007', the s.257 management instrument; the Llandudno Holiday Accommodation Zone and LDP Policy HOU/10, which are planning; and two apparent 'hmo' hits in the raw HTML that turned out to be fragments inside base64-encoded WebResource.axd blobs. LIMITATIONS: Conwy's sitemap.xml is a 3.4KB stub and useless; its content is JavaScript-rendered so raw curl returns navigation only, and the substantive reading was done in a real rendered browser session with the accordions expanded; its ModernGov document search is broken (control query returned a byte-identical empty form to both the real query and the nonsense control), so committee papers could not be full-text searched and the designation dates remain unfound.

schemes.areaDescription: The whole of Denbighshire: any HMO with three or more tenants forming two or more households, plus converted flats that fail the 1991 Building Regulations
Rhyl, Prestatyn, Denbigh and Llangollen; replaced and expanded county-wide by the 2025 scheme

notes: Denbighshire operates county-wide additional HMO licensing from 1 February 2026 to 31 January 2031. Any HMO with three or more tenants forming two or more households needs a licence, anywhere in the county. The basic fee is £890 for five years.
research: ACTIVE and recently expanded. The council's live page states: 'Denbighshire County Council Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2025. On the 21st October 2025, Cabinet approved the Denbighshire County Council Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2025. The areas of Denbigh, Llangollen, Prestatyn and Rhyl have been redesignated for Additional HMO Licensing and the scheme has also been expanded county wide. The scheme will commence on 1 February 2026 and will run for a maximum of five years until 31 January 2031.' The primary designation notice confirms it: 'Notice is hereby given that Denbighshire County Council has on the 21st October 2025 designated a county wide Additional Licensing Scheme... effective from 1st February 2026 and unless revoked beforehand or extended will cease to have effect on 31st January 2031', citing the Wales 2006 Regulations and the Housing Act 2004 (Additional HMO Licensing Wales) General Approval 2007, and catching s.254 HMOs with 'three or more persons, forming two or more households' plus s.257 converted flats. THE PART 2 vs PART 3 QUESTION IS SETTLED OUTRIGHT by the council's own 2025 consultation proposal: 'Section 56 Housing Act 2004 gives power to Local Authorities to designate areas of their district... as subject to additional licensing.' This is s.56, not Part 3. The council sets out the licensable test plainly: 'Under our Additional Licensing Scheme, a HMO property must have a licence if: there are three or more tenants living there AND they form more than one household, with or without shared facilities', expressly contrasted with the mandatory test of 'three or more storeys AND five or more tenants'. THE IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR is recorded as expired: 'on the 28th day of July 2020 designated an Additional Licensing Scheme... covering the electoral wards of Denbigh, Llangollen, Prestatyn and Rhyl... effective from 1st December 2020 and... will cease to have effect on 30th November 2025.' Two earlier Rhyl-area schemes also existed (Cabinet approval 8 September 2009 expiring 31 December 2014; a second designation approved 16 December 2014), but their exact commencement dates are not published, so they are not recorded as dated records rather than asserting inferred dates. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: licences last five years and cost by storeys and habitable rooms, with the ladder STARTING AT 'four or less' habitable rooms (£855/£655/£455 depending on storeys), below the mandatory five-occupant threshold, which is exactly the small-HMO tell of a genuine s.56 scheme. The council's own summary is 'A basic fee of £890 is worked out on the cost for 5 habitable rooms in a building of 3 or more storeys. There is an additional charge of £35 for each habitable room for properties that have between 6 and 10 habitable rooms.' There is also a separate payment route, cost code '3479-40142 (Additional Licence)' versus '3479-40091 (Mandatory Licence)', plus a £200 early-application discount and a 50 per cent charity discount. SELECTIVE LICENSING: none, ever. Zero occurrences across the 4,303-URL sitemap, the full web archive, and every designation and policy document read. WARDS NULL on both records. The 2020 notice calls Denbigh, Llangollen, Prestatyn and Rhyl 'electoral wards', but they are town names that pre-date the 2022 boundary review and do not correspond to current ONS ward names, so coverage 'areas' with wards null is used. The active scheme is county-wide, so no ward list is needed at all. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales; mandatory HMO licensing, which the page correctly separates; the West Rhyl Housing Improvement Project and the West Rhyl regeneration area, which appear only as a ward label on a private-rented-stock chart and are regeneration not designation, and which are the classic Rhyl false lead; all Welsh 'dewisol' hits on the domain, which are discretionary housing payments, discretionary business grants and elective home education; and 'anghenion dysgu ychwanegol' (additional learning needs), the dominant 'ychwanegol' false positive. LIMITATION: WebSearch was unavailable and external engines blocked scripted queries, so every finding rests on direct fetches of denbighshire.gov.uk documents; the same pages were independently located via the council's own sitemap.

schemes.areaDescription: The whole county of Flintshire: any HMO with three or more people in two or more households that is not already mandatory-licensed, plus section 257 converted flats

notes: Flintshire operates county-wide additional HMO licensing from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031, covering smaller HMOs outside mandatory licensing and converted flats. The fee is £849.40 for the first five units plus £38.79 per extra unit. No selective licensing.
research: ACTIVE, brand new, and the strongest-evidenced record in this batch. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR via direct fetch: the page is headed 'Public Notice in Respect of the Introduction of an Additional Licensing Scheme for Houses of Multiple Occupation in Flintshire'. The notice itself is unambiguous: 'This designation is published in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions) (Wales) Regulations 2006. Notice is hereby given that on 14th October 2025, Flintshire County Council designated an Additional Licensing scheme in respect of Houses in Multiple Occupation, which operates in accordance with the Regulations and APPLIES TO THE WHOLE COUNTY. The designation will be known as the "Flintshire County Council Additional Licensing (Houses in Multiple Occupation) Scheme 2026"... The Scheme will be effective from 1st April 2026 and unless revoked beforehand or extended will cease to have effect on 31st March 2031.' The Part 2 vs Part 3 question is settled on the face of the instrument: s.56 to 60, additional, not selective. The Welsh mirror page uses 'trwyddedu YCHWANEGOL' and never 'dewisol' or 'dethol'. SCOPE, quoted: 'The Scheme applies to all Houses in Multiple Occupation (HMOs) within Flintshire, except those exempted by the relevant sections of the HA 2004 and those already licensed under the Mandatory Licensing of Houses in Multiple Occupation Scheme. The Scheme includes properties that meet all of the criteria, within either one of the following two categories: Any type of HMO as defined by Section 254 of the Housing Act 2004 which does not fall within the mandatory licensing scheme, occupied by three or more persons, forming two or more households. HMO properties which are defined within the scope of Section 257 of the Housing Act 2004; HMO's created by converting buildings into flats, but do not meet the 1991 Building Regulations.' The notice also spells out the stakes: 'Failure to apply for a licence where required is an offence under Section 72 of the HA 2004. A person who commits an offence is liable on summary conviction to an unlimited fine... In addition, that person may be required to repay up to 12 months' rent.' FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: the live Licensing Fees and Charges table reads 'HMO Licence Application Fee (For the first 5 Units) £849.40 / HMO (Each Additional Unit) £38.79 / Service of an Enforcement Notice under the Housing Act 2004 £396.68', with the council stating 'The fee has been set on a cost recovery basis in line with government guidance and covers both application processing and inspection.' Cost recovery is the statutory hallmark of a self-financing designation. IMPORTANT FEE CAUTION: 'Units' here means letting units or rooms, NOT occupants, so this is not the five-occupant mandatory-only ladder; and the council publishes no separate mandatory-versus-additional split, so £849.40 plus £38.79 per extra unit is simply what a Flintshire HMO landlord now pays. THIS IS FLINTSHIRE'S FIRST EVER SCHEME. The October 2025 Cabinet report says it 'will bring Flintshire County Council in-line with many other counties in Wales, who have well-established licensing schemes of this sort', and only 14 mandatory HMO licences existed in September 2024. There is consequently no expired predecessor. THE CONNAH'S QUAY, SHOTTON, FLINT AND HOLYWELL ASSOCIATION IS A FALSE LEAD, checked specifically: those are Town Centre Regeneration, SHARP and Place Making programmes, not designations. The scheme is county-wide with no area carve-outs; the only geographic mention in the papers is a consultation respondent's remark about HMO concentration in Deeside. SELECTIVE LICENSING: none. Wayback CDX sweeps show no selective-licensing URL ever existed on the domain. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales; Welsh mandatory HMO licensing under WSI 2006/1712 (W.174); s.254 definitional recitals; statutory power recitals; the per-unit surcharge line, which here sits inside a genuine s.56 scheme rather than standing in for one; and Article 4 and planning permission. The s.257 coverage is NOT the England '(Additional Provisions) (England) Regulations 2007' trap, since the notice cites the Wales 2006 Regulations and s.56 directly. LIMITATIONS: Flintshire's main site search FAILED its control test (byte-identical ~27.9KB shells for 'council tax', 'zzqqxx' and the real query) and was discarded; the committee search failed as GET but worked as POST, where controls passed cleanly. There is no pre-April-2026 archive snapshot of the fee table, so it cannot be proved the £849.40 was introduced with the scheme. Note the council's own misspelling of 'Licencing' in the URL.

schemes.areaDescription: The whole county of Gwynedd, covering every HMO not already caught by mandatory licensing, including Bangor, Caernarfon and Porthmadog

notes: Gwynedd's county-wide additional HMO licence covered all HMOs outside mandatory licensing. The published designation ran to 3 June 2026, but the council still advertises the licence and charges £160 per unit plus £50. Check with Gwynedd before letting an HMO.
research: THE HARDEST CALL IN THIS BATCH, so the reasoning is set out in full. The scheme unquestionably EXISTS and is county-wide s.56 additional licensing. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR via direct fetch, which confirmed the page still reads: 'Additional licence - For all other HMOs Cyngor Gwynedd has decided to make the additional licence relevant to all of Gwynedd to maintain standards. The fee for this licence is £160 per unit in addition to a £50 fee to process the application.' The Welsh page is identical in substance. The statutory public notice linked from that page confirms the power and the dates: 'This notice is published in accordance with Sections 56 to 60 of the Housing Act 2004 and Regulation 9 of the Licensing and Management of Houses in Multiple Occupation and Other Houses (Miscellaneous Provisions)(Wales) Regulations 2006... The designation applies to the whole area of the County of Gwynedd... The designation was made by the Cabinet Member for Housing on the 21.05.2021... The designation will be effective from 04.06.2021 and unless revoked beforehand will CEASE TO HAVE EFFECT ON THE 03.06.2026.' WHY IT IS RECORDED AS EXPIRED: today is 5 August 2026, so the only designation instrument Gwynedd publishes lapsed roughly two months ago, and no re-designation could be found. A companion Revocation Notice on the same page does NOT kill this scheme; it revokes the PREDECESSOR scheme effective 04.06.2021 under Reg 10, reason given 'Designation of a new additional licensing scheme... from the 04.06.2021'. That was checked specifically, because a revocation notice sitting beside a live scheme is an obvious trap. Gwynedd has therefore run rolling county-wide additional licensing for years. WHY THIS IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN TREATED AS SETTLED: the council UPDATED BOTH LANGUAGE VERSIONS OF THE PAGE ON 11 JUNE 2026, after expiry, and still presents the additional licence as current and still quotes its fee. Weighing that: the PDF internal timestamps show both notices were merely re-saved on 09.06.2026 against 2021 creation dates, consistent with the bulk CMS migration that moved /en/ paths to /en-gb/ rather than a substantive update; the asset-library copy is byte-identical by MD5; Wayback holds only one snapshot (2022) with a different digest, so there is no history to diff; and six plausible new-notice filenames under both document paths all returned 404. Gwynedd's ModernGov was searched across 30 meetings of Cabinet and Communities Scrutiny for January 2025 to October 2026 with zero matches for trwydd, licen, amlddeiliad, HMO, dewisol or ychwanegol; that scan is CONTROL-VALIDATED, since the same parser extracts real agenda items from Cabinet on 9 June 2026. HOWEVER the 2021 designation was made by the Cabinet Member individually rather than by Cabinet, and Gwynedd's officer and member decisions register returned 'No matching decisions' for every date range tried, which is not trustworthy. So a renewal by delegated decision is plausible and could not be excluded. Because the harm of under-warning is severe (s.72(1) carries an unlimited fine plus a rent repayment order), the public note deliberately tells landlords the council is still advertising and charging for the licence and to check before letting, rather than implying they are clear. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST: passed strongly. A distinct additional-licence fee of £160 per unit plus £50 processing is published in both languages, precisely the separate cost-recovery signal a genuine s.56 scheme must carry. SELECTIVE LICENSING: none exists or has been proposed. TRAPS EXCLUDED: Rent Smart Wales; mandatory 3-storey/5-person licensing under WSI 2006/1712 (W.174), which the page keeps expressly separate; Article 4 directions and second-home planning policy; Gwynedd's high second-home and empty-home council tax premiums, which are tax not licensing and are a strong local distractor; the s.254 definition; and the Welsh homonyms 'taliadau-tai-dewisol-dhp' (Discretionary Housing Payments) and 'tai-gofal-ychwanegol' (Extra Care Housing). LIMITATIONS, all control-tested: ModernGov mgDelegatedDecisions ignores TitleContains; ieSearchResults 404s on POST and returns byte-identical responses for the control, the nonsense query and the real query; and the site search reports '1024 results' for the nonsense control exactly as for 'council tax'. None of those nil results is relied on. A direct call to Gwynedd's Private Rented Sector Unit is the one step that would close this gap and no automated route could substitute for it.

notes: Anglesey has no selective or additional licensing scheme. Only mandatory HMO licensing applies: three or more storeys with five or more people in two or more households. Fee £749, renewal £557.50. All landlords in Wales must also register with Rent Smart Wales.
research: NEGATIVE, triangulated four ways. The council's HMO page states verbatim: 'Licensing is mandatory for all HMOs which have three or more storeys and are occupied by five or more persons forming two or more households.' The Welsh page matches. That is the mandatory threshold only, with no 'all other HMOs' extension of the kind Gwynedd publishes next door. The full page was read in raw HTML and contains ZERO occurrences of 'additional licen', 'selective licen', 'ychwanegol' or 'dewisol'. The council's own public register is titled 'Register of mandatory houses in multiple occupation licences', the word 'mandatory' being the council's own, and there is no parallel additional-licence register. FEE-SCHEDULE TEST, decisive: Anglesey's live 'Council fees and charges from 1 April 2026' schedule, a 51-page document, contains exactly three HMO lines: 'Houses in Multiple Occupation MANDATORY Licence Application Fee £749.00'; 'Houses in Multiple Occupation MANDATORY Licence Renewal Fee £557.50'; 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Public Register £64.50'. There is no additional-licensing fee and no selective-licensing fee anywhere in the 51 pages, and a live scheme must be self-financing. All 39 occurrences of 'additional' in that document were checked and every one is an unrelated surcharge, the classic false positive. Zero occurrences of 'selective'. SITEMAP SWEEP: all 2,523 URLs parsed and grepped raw for 'selectiv', 'dewisol', 'ychwanegol', 'trwydd', 'HMO' and 'amlfeddiannaeth'. No licensing-scheme page exists, and Anglesey's licences-and-permits tree has no housing or residential licence branch at all, unlike Gwynedd's; HMO work sits under environmental health. TRAPS EXCLUDED AND NAMED: Rent Smart Wales, for which Anglesey has two dedicated pages and to which the HMO page directs landlords at its close, the dominant Welsh false positive; the s.254 definitional paragraphs, which run to four bullet descriptions on this page; the linked gov.wales tenant guidance whose anchor text reads 'councils... have powers to require licensing of other HMOs', a statutory-powers recital describing the power not its exercise; the £64.50 public-register fee, which is s.232 cost recovery for supplying a copy of the register and is NOT a licensing fee; council tax premiums on second and empty homes, a major local issue but tax not licensing; Article 4 and conservation-area planning rules; and the Welsh homonyms 'Anghenion Dysgu Ychwanegol', 'Rhyddhad dewisol', 'Thaliadau Tai Dewisol', 'Addysg ddewisol yn y cartref' and 'Rheolau cynllunio ychwanegol', which together account for every single 'dewisol' and 'ychwanegol' hit on the domain. REACHABILITY: no 403s encountered; anglesey.gov.wales redirects to anglesey.gov.uk, which serves canonical content on both /en/ and /cy/ paths.
